statutory_acts.title: Traditional Knowledge Exclusion Bar
statutory_acts.summary: Inventions that are essentially traditional knowledge or an aggregation of known properties of traditionally known components are non-patentable.
statutory_acts.text: An invention which in effect is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components is not an invention within the meaning of this Act. Classical Ayurvedic formulations sourced from recognized texts in the First Schedule to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act fall directly under this statutory bar unless substantial synergistic or non-obvious technical effect is proven.
statutory_acts.applicability: Applies to all Ayurvedic, Siddha, and Unani formulations and natural herbal extracts.

statutory_acts.title: Efficacy Enhancement Requirement
statutory_acts.summary: New forms of known substances or mere combinations must demonstrate significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy.
statutory_acts.text: The mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy of that substance or the mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance or of the mere use of a known process, machine or apparatus unless such known process results in a new product or employs at least one new reactant is not patentable. For herbal formulations, comparative pharmacological or clinical trial data proving unexpected synergy is mandatory to overcome Section 3(d).
statutory_acts.applicability: Combinations, extracts, salts, esters, or polymorphs of known phytochemical compounds.

statutory_acts.title: Mere Admixture Bar
statutory_acts.summary: A substance obtained by mere mixing of components resulting only in aggregation of properties is non-patentable.
statutory_acts.text: A substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance is not patentable. An applicant must demonstrate synergy where Combination Effect > Sum of Individual Effects (e.g., Combination Index < 1.0 or significant bioavailability enhancement).
statutory_acts.applicability: Polyherbal mixtures, decoctions, and dietary supplements.

statutory_acts.title: Mandatory Biological Resource Disclosure
statutory_acts.summary: Applicants must declare the source and geographical origin of any biological resource used in the specification.
statutory_acts.text: Every complete specification must disclose the source and geographical origin of the biological material in the specification when used in an invention. Failure to disclose or wrongful disclosure is a specific ground for pre-grant opposition under Section 25(1)(j), post-grant opposition under Section 25(2)(j), and revocation under Section 64(1)(p).
statutory_acts.applicability: Any patent specification utilizing herbs, plants, seeds, or microbial material from India.

statutory_acts.title: Term of Patent & Maintenance
statutory_acts.summary: Term is 20 years from international/provisional filing date; subject to renewal fee payment.
statutory_acts.text: The term of every patent granted, after the commencement of the Patents (Amendment) Act 2002, and the term of every patent which has not expired and has not ceased to have effect, shall be twenty years from the date of filing of the application for the patent. Renewal fees must be paid annually from the 3rd year onwards to prevent lapse.

statutory_acts.title: Access to Biological Resources by Non-Indian Entities
statutory_acts.summary: Non-Indian persons, foreign entities, or Indian companies with foreign shareholding require prior NBA approval for biological resources.
statutory_acts.text: No person who is not a citizen of India, or an entity incorporated or registered in India having any non-Indian participation in its share capital or management, shall without prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority obtain any biological resource occurring in India or knowledge associated thereto for research or commercial utilization or bio-survey and bio-utilization.
statutory_acts.applicability: Foreign collaborations, export of Ayurvedic plants, and MNC pharmaceutical firms.

statutory_acts.title: NBA Approval Prior to Patent Grant (Form I)
statutory_acts.summary: Approval of NBA is mandatory prior to grant of patent inside or outside India based on Indian biological resources.
statutory_acts.text: Under Section 6, as amended in 2023, prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority must be obtained before the grant of the patent (rather than before filing), by filing NBA Form I. Benefit sharing typically entails 0.1% to 0.5% of annual gross ex-factory sales or 5% of licensing royalty. Registered AYUSH practitioners and codified traditional knowledge manufacturers have codified exemptions for domestic manufacture.
statutory_acts.applicability: All patent applications based on Indian medicinal flora (e.g. Ashwagandha, Turmeric, Neem, Brahmi).

statutory_acts.title: Ayurvedic Drug Regulatory Categories
statutory_acts.summary: Classifies Ayurvedic products into Classical (Generic), Patent & Proprietary (P&P), and Phytopharmaceuticals.
statutory_acts.text: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, Ayurvedic drugs are categorized into: 1. Classical / Generic formulations: manufactured strictly in accordance with recognized ancient classical texts listed in the First Schedule (Form 25D license, no trial needed); 2. Patent or Proprietary (P&P) Ayurvedic medicines: containing First Schedule ingredients formulated into modern dosage forms (requires Rule 158B safety and published efficacy data); 3. Phytopharmaceuticals: purified bioactive fractions requiring CDSCO New Drug clinical trials (Phases I-IV).
statutory_acts.applicability: Determines manufacturing licenses, clinical trial burden, and marketing authorization.

statutory_acts.title: Ayurveda Aahar (Nutraceuticals) Regulatory Framework
statutory_acts.summary: Food products prepared in accordance with Ayurvedic texts for dietary health without disease cure claims.
statutory_acts.text: Regulations governing foods prepared using processes and recipes described in recognized Ayurvedic texts. Such products carry the dedicated 'Ayurveda Aahar' logo. They may promote general health, digestion, and vitality, but are legally prohibited from claiming treatment, mitigation, or cure of specific human diseases.
statutory_acts.applicability: Herbal teas, rasayanas, energy mixes, dietary supplements, and botanical nutritionals.

statutory_acts.title: Withania somnifera (Ashwagandha) Churna Formulation
statutory_acts.summary: Classical Rasayana formulation for balya (strength), debility, and stress reduction recorded from Charaka Samhita.
statutory_acts.text: TKDL Record AY-0417 cites Charaka Samhita, Chikitsasthanam Chapter 1: Ashwagandha root powder mixed with ghrita (clarified butter) and ksheera (cow milk) indicated for Daurbalya (General Debility) and Karshya (Emaciation). Cited successfully against 14 foreign patent attempts claiming Ashwagandha extracts for stress or muscle strength.
statutory_acts.applicability: Direct prior art conflict under Section 3(p) for generic Ashwagandha formulations.

statutory_acts.title: Curcuma longa (Haridra) Khanda & Piper nigrum Synergy
statutory_acts.summary: Classical combination of turmeric with black pepper (Maricha) and long pepper (Pippali) for anti-inflammatory & respiratory use.
statutory_acts.text: TKDL Record AY-0922 cites Bhaishajya Ratnavali, Udardapratishedha Adhyaya: Haridra Khanda comprising Curcuma longa processed with Trikatu (Piper nigrum, Piper longum, Zingiber officinale) for Kandu (pruritus), Sheetapitta (urticaria), and Shwasa (bronchial inflammation). Known prior art for piperine-curcumin bio-enhancement; patenting requires proving non-obvious synergistic ratio or novel nanocarrier.
statutory_acts.applicability: Overcoming Section 3(p) requires proving unexpected bioavailability ratio (e.g. 50:1 to 100:1) with clinical pharmacokinetic profile.

statutory_acts.title: Triphala Formulation (Amalaki, Haritaki, Bibhitaki)
statutory_acts.summary: Classical Chakshushya (ophthalmic health) and rasayana formulation cited from Sushruta Samhita.
statutory_acts.text: TKDL Record AY-1289 records equal proportion mixture of Emblica officinalis, Terminalia chebula, and Terminalia bellirica as Triphala Kwatha for ocular cleansing, digestion, and oxidative balance. Prior art defeats broad claims for general antioxidant eye drops; novel supercritical fluid or micro-emulsion delivery claims remain eligible.
statutory_acts.applicability: Prevents patenting of standard Triphala extracts; requires novel drug delivery system (NDDS).

statutory_acts.title: Patentable Subject Matter & Plant Exclusions
statutory_acts.summary: Members may exclude plants, animals, and biological processes, but must provide plant variety protection.
statutory_acts.text: TRIPS Article 27.3(b) allows WTO member states to exclude from patentability plants and animals other than micro-organisms, and essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals. Members must provide for the protection of plant varieties either by patents or by an effective sui generis system (in India, PPV&FR Act 2001).
statutory_acts.applicability: Determines international patent scope for botanical extracts versus cultivated varieties.

statutory_acts.title: Prior Informed Consent & Fair Access Benefit Sharing
statutory_acts.summary: Access to genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge requires PIC and mutually agreed terms.
statutory_acts.text: Parties must ensure that benefits arising from the utilization of genetic resources as well as subsequent applications and commercialization are shared in a fair and equitable manner with the provider country upon Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT). Access requires Prior Informed Consent (PIC). Crucial for Indian exporters filing patents in US, Europe, or Japan.
statutory_acts.applicability: International filings involving Ayurvedic biological resources sourced from India.

statutory_acts.title: PCT International Filing & National Phase Deadline
statutory_acts.summary: Single international filing gives 30/31 months from priority date to enter national phases worldwide.
statutory_acts.text: A PCT application allows an Indian applicant to preserve worldwide priority filing rights across 157 contracting states. The applicant has 30 or 31 months from the initial Indian priority date to enter national phase examination in designated target offices (e.g. USPTO, EPO, JPO, CNIPA). Indian applicants filing abroad must obtain Section 39 foreign filing permission if filed outside India first.
statutory_acts.applicability: Global expansion for Ayurvedic pharmaceutical and biotech innovations.

statutory_acts.title: US Subject Matter Eligibility & Products of Nature Bar
statutory_acts.summary: Naturally occurring botanicals are ineligible under Section 101 unless markedly different characteristics are proven.
statutory_acts.text: Under the US Supreme Court Mayo/Myriad precedents and 35 U.S.C. §101, natural plant extracts are unpatentable as 'products of nature' unless the inventor demonstrates that the extract possesses 'markedly different characteristics' (e.g. synthetic structural modification, specific non-natural synergistic ratio, or specialized nanoparticle formulation).
statutory_acts.applicability: Filing Ayurvedic patents in the United States.

statutory_acts.title: Novelty & Inventive Step (Problem-Solution Approach)
statutory_acts.summary: Claims must demonstrate non-obvious technical effect over TKDL prior art citing Charaka or Sushruta Samhita.
statutory_acts.text: Under the European Patent Convention, inventions must be novel and involve an inventive step evaluated via the Problem-Solution Approach. The EPO has a formal cooperation agreement with CSIR-TKDL; examiners routinely search TKDL records. To satisfy Article 56, the applicant must demonstrate surprising technical effect not foreshadowed in Ayurvedic classical texts.
statutory_acts.applicability: Filing Ayurvedic inventions across 39 European member states.

official_forms.name: Application for Grant of Patent
official_forms.description: Statutory application identifying applicant, inventors, title, provisional/complete specification, and declaration of biological material source.

official_forms.name: Provisional or Complete Specification
official_forms.deadline: 12 months to file Complete if Provisional filed
official_forms.description: Full technical disclosure including Title, Field, Prior Art background, Summary, Working Examples, Synergistic Efficacy Data, Claims 1-10, and Abstract.

official_forms.name: Statement and Undertaking regarding Foreign Applications
official_forms.deadline: Within 6 months of filing foreign applications (Section 8)
official_forms.description: Mandatory disclosure under Section 8 of all corresponding patent applications filed in foreign jurisdictions (USPTO, EPO, PCT).

official_forms.name: Declaration as to Inventorship
official_forms.deadline: With complete specification or within 1 month
official_forms.description: Formal attestation that the named researchers are the true and first inventors of the Ayurvedic innovation.

official_forms.name: Request for Early Publication
official_forms.description: Accelerates official publication from 18 months down to approximately 1 month, enabling earlier commercial licensing and examination request.

official_forms.name: Request for Expedited Examination
official_forms.description: Fast-track examination available for Startups, MSMEs, female applicants, and entities utilizing Indian biological resources, granting first examination report (FER) within months.

official_forms.name: Application for NBA Prior Approval for IPR
official_forms.deadline: Mandatory prior to grant of patent (BDA 2023 Section 6)
official_forms.description: Statutory application under Section 6 of Biological Diversity Act for permission to commercialize patent based on Indian biological resources, establishing benefit sharing terms.

official_forms.name: Manufacturing License for Ayurvedic/Siddha Drugs
official_forms.deadline: Prior to commercial manufacture or clinical distribution
official_forms.description: Regulatory license under Drugs & Cosmetics Act for manufacturing Classical formulations or Patent & Proprietary medicines in a GMP-certified facility.
